blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Terminal agents act through stochastic model generations, yet the ability to generate a useful action does not ensure its reliable execution.
A poor command ( e.g., wrong package install) can change the environment in ways that hinder subsequent progress, even when the model could generate a better alternative.
We investigate whether allocating test-time compute at the model-harness boundary can improve action reliability and trajectory success, and what makes this allocation effective.
To study these questions, we introduce Mid-Harness , which samples and verifies candidate actions before forwarding one for execution, while keeping the generator and harness unchanged.
With a TMAX-9B generator, more action sampling yields little benefit under weak verification, whereas a capable verifier can exploit useful alternatives from the same generator.
On TerminalBench-Lite, a GPT-5.6 Sol verifier raises Pass@1 from 50.00% for the base agent to 68.03% with 8 sampled actions.
When the same TMAX-9B model serves as the verifier, pairwise verification performs best among the evaluated verification mechanisms.
Distilling responses from the stronger verifier into TMAX-9B further improves Pass@1, while leaving the action generator unchanged.
With TMAX-9B on TerminalBench-Lite, combining action and trajectory scaling reaches higher success at lower estimated token cost than generating more trajectories alone.
Mid-Harness also improves performance across additional models, benchmarks, and harnesses.
These findings identify action scaling as a promising target for test-time compute scaling in terminal agents. The project page is available at link .

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Large language models increasingly power terminal agents that perform tasks in software engineering, data science, and scientific discovery [ 4 , 5 ] .
Yet the ability to generate useful actions does not ensure that an agent completes a task reliably.
The same model and harness may succeed on one run and fail on another because each run commits to a long-horizon sequence of stochastically generated actions.
Each executed command changes the environment on which subsequent decisions depend [ 6 , 7 , 8 ] .
Therefore, a poor command ( e.g., wrong code edit, wrong package install) can hinder subsequent progress by changing the environment, even when the model could have generated a better alternative [ 9 ] .
We use action reliability to mean consistently generating actions that support task completion, and evaluate its trajectory-level consequences through task success.
blocks.zh:
大型语言模型日益增强在软件工程,数据科学,和科学发现等方面执行任务的动力终端代理[4,5].
然而,产生有用行动的能力并不能确保代理人可靠地完成任务。
同样的模式和手段在一次运行中可能成功,而在另一次运行中则可能失败,因为每次运行都承诺采取长距离的、有条理的行动。
每个执行的命令都会改变随后决定所依赖的环境[6,7,8].
因此,一个差的命令(例如错误的代码编辑,错误的包安装)可以通过改变环境来阻碍后续的进展,即使模型本可以产生更好的替代[9].
我们使用行动可靠性来表示一贯产生支持完成任务的行动,并通过任务成功评价其轨迹层面的后果。

blocks.en:
Prior work improves reasoning and agent performance by allocating additional test-time compute to sampling, verification, and refinement [ 10 , 11 , 12 , 3 , 2 ] , including verification of candidate actions before execution [ 13 , 14 ] .
These successes motivate scaling compute for action reliability, but leave an incomplete understanding of when and why this scaling improves trajectory success.
In particular, the benefit of generating more candidates depends on the ability to verify them, making it important to study these factors jointly [ 15 ] .
We therefore conduct a systematic study of action sampling and verification, asking: when does additional computation before action execution improve trajectory success, and what makes it effective?
blocks.zh:
先前的工作改进了推理和代理性能,将额外的试验时间计算用于取样、核查和完善[10、11、12、3、2],包括在执行前核查候选行动[13、14]。
这些成功激励了对行动可靠性的计算,但对何时和为什么这种计算能改善轨迹的成功留下了不完全的了解。
特别是,产生更多候选人的好处取决于核实他们的能力,因此必须共同研究这些因素[15]。
因此,我们对行动取样和核查进行系统研究,问:行动执行前的额外计算何时能提高轨迹的成功程度?

blocks.en:
To investigate these questions, we introduce Mid-Harness , a method for studying action-level compute scaling at the model-harness boundary while keeping the action generator and execution harness unchanged ( Mid-Harness: Scaling Actions Between Model and Harness for Terminal Agents (a)).
At each step, Mid-Harness requests several candidate actions from the generator using the same interaction history, applies a verifier, and forwards only the chosen candidate to the harness for execution.
Our main comparisons vary candidate width, verification mechanism, and verifier capability with TMAX-9B [ 1 ] and its harness fixed.
We use these comparisons to study two requirements: whether the generator provides useful alternatives, and whether verification can identify them before execution [ 16 ] .
blocks.zh:
为了调查这些问题,我们引入了中Harness(中Harness:在模型和终端代理之间放大动作),这是一种在模型和模型的边界上研究动作层面计算缩放的方法,同时保持动作生成器和执行控制装置不变(中Harness:在模型和终端代理之间放大动作(a))。
每一步,中Harness都会要求生成器使用相同的交互历史进行若干个候选动作,应用一个验证符,并且只将选定的候选符转发给使用器执行.
与TMAX-9B[1]相比,我们的主要比较范围、核查机制、核查能力各不相同,而且固定了核查能力。
我们利用这些比较来研究两项要求:生成器是否提供有用的替代品,以及核查是否能够在执行之前识别这些替代品[16]。

blocks.en:
We first ask whether the generator already produces useful alternatives that could improve trajectory success if reliably identified.
Without ground-truth labels for candidate actions, we probe this opportunity using a strong verifier.
With TMAX-9B as the fixed generator on TerminalBench-Lite [ 17 ] , verification by GPT-5.6 Sol [ 18 ] raises Pass@1 from 50.00% for the base agent to 68.03% ( Mid-Harness: Scaling Actions Between Model and Harness for Terminal Agents (b)).
This result provides evidence that the generator produces useful alternatives that verification can exploit, improving trajectory success without changing or further post-training the generator.
blocks.zh:
我们首先要问,发电机是否已经产生有用的替代办法,如果可靠地确定,可以改善轨道的成功。
没有可选行动的地面真实标签,我们利用强有力的核查员来探寻这一机会。
由于TMAX-9B是Bench-Lite终端的固定生成器[17],通过GPT-5.6 Sol [18]的验证,Pass@1的基质代理从50.0%提升到68.03%(中Harness:Model和Harness之间的动作放大终端代理(b)).
这一结果提供了证据,证明发电机产生有用的替代物,可以加以核查,改进轨迹成功,而不改变或进一步培训发电机。

blocks.en:
We next examine how much of this opportunity can be recovered in a self-verification setting, where the same model generates and verifies actions.
We find that increasing candidate width yields marginal improvement under weak verification ( Section 4 ).
In this setting, pairwise verification performs best among the evaluated mechanisms, showing that how candidates are compared matters even without changing the verifier model ( Figure 2 ).
Fine-tuning a verifier initialized from the generator on pairwise responses from GPT-5.6 Sol further raises Pass@1 from 54.76% to 57.14%, while leaving the action generator unchanged ( Section 4.3 ).
Our analysis shows that distillation increases offline agreement with the frontier verifier, while disagreement over command semantics and execution feasibility persists ( Section 5 ).
Together, these results identify verifying what an action will do in the current environment without executing it as a central challenge in converting candidate diversity into successful trajectories.
blocks.zh:
我们接下来审查在自我核查的情况下,在同一个模式产生和核实行动的情况下,可以恢复多少这一机会。
我们发现,在核查不力的情况下,候选人的宽度的提高略有改善(第4节)。
在此情况下,双向核查在被评价的机制中表现最好,表明即使不改变核查模式,如何对候选人进行比较(图2)。
根据GPT-5.6的对偶反应,对生成器初始化的核查器进行微调。 Sol进一步将Pass@1从54.76%提高到57.14%,同时使动作生成器保持不变(第4.3节)。
我们的分析表明,蒸馏会增加与边境核查员的离线协议,而对指令语义和执行可行性的分歧仍然存在(第5节)。
这些结果共同确定了在目前环境中核查一项行动将采取的行动,而不将其作为将候选人多样性转化为成功轨迹的一项核心挑战加以执行。

blocks.en:
Finally, we investigate whether the benefits of action scaling extend to trajectory-level compute scaling methods.
On TerminalBench-Lite, Mid-Harness improves Pass@1 with both parallel scaling using Best-of- T T Trajectories with an LLM-as-a-verifier [ 2 ] and sequential scaling using Sequential Refine [ 3 ] ( Mid-Harness: Scaling Actions Between Model and Harness for Terminal Agents (b), Section 6.1 ).
With TMAX-9B, combining Mid-Harness with one round of SR surpasses Best-of- T T at T = 7 T=7 while using less than half its estimated token cost ( Figure 6 ).
We also find gains across additional models, tasks, and harnesses ( Section 6.2 ).
blocks.zh:
最后,我们调查行动规模的效益是否延伸到轨迹一级的计算规模方法。
在终端Bench-Lite上,中Harness改进了Pass@1,同时使用具有LLM-as-a-验证器的Best-Of-T T轨距进行平行缩放[2],并使用Sequential Evenine[3]进行顺序缩放(中Harness:用于终端代理的模型和效果之间的动作缩放(b),第6.1节)。
与TMAX-9B结合,将中Harness与一回合SR在T=7 T=7时超越最佳TT,同时使用不到一半的估计代币成本(图6).
我们还通过其他模式、任务和手段找到好处(第6.2节)。

blocks.en:
Our main findings and contributions are: • Verification governs the benefit of action sampling. With TMAX-9B on TerminalBench-Lite, wider sampling yields little benefit under weak verification, while the strong verifier enables substantially more successful trajectories. • Verification mechanism and training help recover this opportunity. Pairwise verification performs best among the evaluated mechanisms, and verifier distillation improves trajectory success without changing the generator.
The offline analysis identifies command semantics and execution feasibility as persistent sources of disagreement with the teacher verifier. • Mid-Harness enables a systematic study of action scaling in terminal agents. By varying sampling and verification at a fixed model-harness boundary, we examine when additional computation improves trajectory success and demonstrate its compatibility with parallel and sequential trajectory scaling.

Comparing candidates against the unresolved task requirement may therefore improve both the next action and the states encountered later, while requiring only one environment instance [ 13 ] .

因此,将候选人与尚未解决的任务要求进行比较,既可以改进下一步行动,也可以改进后来遇到的国家,同时只需要一个环境实例[13]。

blocks.en: 3 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 3 实验设置

blocks.en: We evaluate what makes action scaling effective, whether distillation improves verification, and how this scaling axis composes with compute spent across complete runs.
blocks.zh: 我们评价是什么使得行动规模有效,蒸馏是否改进了核查,以及这个缩放轴如何用整个运行的计算来构成。

blocks.en:
The main evaluation uses TerminalBench Lite [ 17 , 5 ] with a TMAX-9B generator [ 1 ] and the Vanillux2 harness. TMAX-9B is trained from Qwen3.5-9B [ 25 ] through reinforcement learning on synthetic terminal tasks using Vanillux2.
Model-scale experiments additionally use TMAX-4B and TMAX-27B.
The generator samples at temperature 0.8 with at most 64 steps, a maximum 65,536 token context, and a 16,384 token output limit per step.
Unless otherwise specified, the verifier uses the same language model as the generator.
The frontier verifier in Section 4.1 uses GPT-5.6 Sol [ 18 ] .
blocks.zh:
主评价使用终端Bench Lite [17, 5] 配备一台TMAX-9B生成器 [1] 和 Vanillux2 牵引装置. TMAX-9B通过使用Vanillux2对合成终端任务的强化学习,从Quen3.5-9B[25]开始训练.
模型尺度实验额外使用TMAX-4B和TMAX-27B.
发电机在0.8温度下取样,最多为64步,最大为65,536令牌上下文,每步16,384令牌输出限制.
除非另有说明,核查员使用与生成器相同的语言模型.
第4.1节中的边界核查员使用GPT-5.6 Sol [18].

blocks.en:
A run is one execution on a task, and its trajectory is the resulting sequence of actions and observations.
We evaluate three runs per task and report Pass@1 as the average exact-success rate across those runs. Pass@3 measures the fraction of tasks solved by at least one of the three runs.
For Best-of- T T , Pass@1 evaluates the returned output for each task.
More evaluation details are in Appendix B.1 .
blocks.zh:
跑步是一次任务上的一次执行,其轨迹是由此而来的行动和观察的顺序.
我们评价每项任务三次运行,并将Pass@1报告为这些运行的平均准确成功率。 Pass@3 测量三个运行中至少一个运行完成的部分任务.
对于Best-of-T T, Pass@1评价每个任务的返回输出.
附录B.1载有更多的评价细节。

blocks.en:
The base agent executes one sampled action per step in a single run, without additional action verification or trajectory scaling.
We organize additional compute at two levels: before action execution and across complete runs.
blocks.zh:
基质在一次运行中每步执行一次抽样动作,没有附加动作验证或轨迹缩放.
我们组织在两个层面进行额外计算:行动执行之前和整个运行过程。

blocks.en:
The action-level axis applies zero-shot or distilled Mid-Harness inside a run.
Zero-shot Mid-Harness uses the same generator model as the verifier without any fine-tuning, while distilled Mid-Harness uses a verifier with the model fine-tuned on pairwise comparisons from GPT-5.6 Sol as described in Section 4.3 .
At the trajectory level, Best-of- T T Trajectories (Best-of- T T ) uses a probabilistic pivot tournament to choose one output from T T completed trajectories [ 2 ] .
The corresponding TMAX model serves as the trajectory verifier at each model scale.
The sequential trajectory-level method Sequential Refine (SR) [ 3 , 12 ] performs R R refinement rounds, each summarizing the previous run to guide a fresh run.
The corresponding TMAX model produces the trajectory summary.
Further baseline details are provided in Appendix B.1 .

动作级轴在运行中采用零射法或衍射的中Harness.
Zero-shot Mid-Harness使用与验证器相同的发电机型号而没有任何微调,而蒸馏的中Harness则使用一个在GPT-5.6 Sol的对等比较上微调模型的验证器. 第4.3节描述.

相应的TMAX模型作为每个模型尺度的轨迹验证器.
相继的轨迹水平方法 R R 改进回合,每回合总结前一次运行以引导新运行.
相应的TMAX模型产生轨迹摘要.

blocks.en: 4 When Does Action Scaling Work?
blocks.zh: 4 行动扩大何时有效?

blocks.en: We examine when sampling and verification improve trajectory success, their costs, and the effect of verifier distillation, with a fixed TMAX-9B generator.
blocks.zh: 我们审查取样和核查时如何改进轨迹的成功、其成本以及使用固定的TMAX-9B发电机进行核查的蒸馏的效果。

blocks.en: 4.1 Candidate Coverage
blocks.zh: 4.1 候选人覆盖率

blocks.en:
We test whether sampled actions contain useful alternatives by pairing the fixed TMAX-9B generator with GPT-5.6 Sol [ 18 ] .
Candidate coverage concerns whether sampled actions include useful alternatives. Without action-level ground truth, we probe it indirectly through trajectory success under a strong verifier. As shown in Figure 2 , this configuration reaches 64.63% Pass@1 at N = 4 N=4 and 68.03% at N = 8 N=8 , showing that the generator’s action candidates support substantially more reliable trajectories.
We next ask how much of this opportunity self-verification can recover.
blocks.zh:
我们通过将固定的TMAX-9B生成器与GPT-5.6 Sol [18] 配对,来检验抽样行动是否包含有用的替代品。
候选人的覆盖面涉及抽样行动是否包括有用的替代办法。 没有行动层面的地面真相,我们在一个强大的验证器下通过轨迹成功间接地探测它. 如图2所示,这种配置在N=4 N=4时达到64.63%的Pass@1,在N=8 N=8时达到68.03%,表明生成器的动作候选人支持的轨迹要大得多可靠.
我们接下来问,这一自我核查的机会有多少可以恢复。

blocks.en: 4.2 Candidate Width and Verification
blocks.zh: 4.2 候选人的宽度和核实

blocks.en:
Under zero-shot listwise verification, doubling the width from N = 4 N=4 to N = 8 N=8 changes Pass@1 only from 49.32% to 51.02% and Pass@3 from 66.33% to 67.35% ( Figure 2 ).
The frontier verifier uses the same listwise mechanism but achieves substantially higher success ( Section 4.1 ).
This contrast suggests that the weaker zero-shot verifier struggles to distinguish useful actions when comparing the full candidate set at once, so additional candidates alone offer little benefit.
blocks.zh:
在零镜头列表验证下,将宽度从N=4 N=4翻倍到N=8 N=8 改变Pass@1,仅从49.32%变为51.02%,Pass@3从66.33%变为67.35%(图2)。
前沿核查员采用同样的列表机制,但取得了显著更高的成功(第4.1节)。
这一对比表明,较弱的零射线核查员在一次比较所设置的全部候选人时难以区分有用的行动,因此仅靠其他候选人就没有什么好处。

blocks.en: With the generator and N = 8 N=8 fixed, pointwise improves Pass@1 only slightly over listwise and leaves Pass@3 unchanged, while pairwise reaches 54.76% Pass@1 and 71.43% Pass@3 ( Figure 2 ).
blocks.zh: 发电机和N=8 N=8固定后,点向改进的Pass@1仅略高于列表,而Pass@3不变,双向修正的Pass@1和71.43%Pass@3(图2)。

blocks.en: 4.3 Verifier Distillation
blocks.zh: 4.3 验证器蒸发

blocks.en:
The frontier verifier result reveals a substantial gap between GPT-5.6 Sol and the generator model (TMAX-9B) as a verifier.
We test whether supervised distillation can transfer part of this capability without serving the frontier model at inference time [ 26 ] .
Using 117k frontier-verifier pairwise responses collected from 732 trajectories across 244 difficult TMAX-15k tasks [ 1 ] , we use LoRA [ 27 ] to train a verifier to generate the GPT-5.6 Sol teacher’s reasoning, scores, and preference label.
Fine-tuned LoRA is only activated for the verifier, not the generator.
Training data and optimization details are provided in Appendix B.3 .
blocks.zh:
前沿核查结果显示,GPT-5.6 Sol与作为核查器的生成器模型(TMAX-9B)之间存在很大差距。
我们检验有监督的蒸馏是否能够在推论时间不为前沿模型服务的情况下转移部分这种能力。
使用从732个轨迹中收集到的117k前沿验证器双向对齐反应,
微调的LORA只用于验证器,而不是生成器.
培训数据和优化细节见附录B.3。

blocks.en:
As shown in Figure 2 , distillation at N = 8 N=8 raises Pass@1 from 54.76% to 57.14% and Pass@3 from 71.43% to 75.51% for pairwise verification.
The improvement also appears at N = 4 N=4 , where Pass@1 rises from 54.42% to 55.44% and Pass@3 rises from 68.37% to 70.41%.
Even the strongest evaluated zero-shot mechanism leaves room for improvement: verifier distillation raises trajectory success without changing the generator.
We next examine which pairwise preferences distillation improves and which remain difficult ( Section 5 ).
blocks.zh:
如图2所示,在N=8 N=8时的蒸馏将Pass@1从54.76%提高到57.14%,将Pass@3从71.43%提高到75.51%,用于对等验证。
N=4 N=4也出现了改善,Pass@1从54.42%上升到55.44%,Pass@3从68.37%上升到70.41%.
即使是最强的经评价的零射机理也留有改进的余地:核查器蒸馏在不改变发电机的情况下提高轨迹成功.
接下来,我们将审查哪些双向偏好蒸馏改进了,哪些仍然困难(第5节)。

On the left, widening from N = 4 N=4 to N = 8 N=8 increases generator POT since the longest of more sampled generations tends to be longer.

blocks.en:
Does effective action verification require explicit reasoning generation [ 24 ] ?
Following direct prediction in discriminative reward models [ 21 , 28 ] , we evaluate pairwise verifiers that emit only an A / B preference (Decision-only setting), using the zero-shot model or a model distilled for one-token responses.
At N = 8 N=8 , both TMAX-9B decision-only verifiers improve Pass@1 over their reasoning counterparts while lowering reference-priced token cost by 20.9% and 24.1% for zero-shot and distilled verification, respectively ( Table 8 ).
At 4B and 27B, the evaluated decision-only variants have lower estimated token cost but also lower Pass@1 than their reasoning counterparts ( Table 8 ).
Additional Pass@3 and N = 4 N=4 results appear in Appendix C.1 .
blocks.zh:
有效行动核查是否需要明确的推理生成[24]?
在对区别奖励模型进行直接预测[21,28]之后,我们评价只发出A/B偏好(仅决定设置)的双向验证器,使用零射量模型或为单键反应而蒸馏的模型。
在N = 8 N = 8时,TMAX-9B只限决定验证器将Pass@1改进于其推理对应器,同时将参考价代币成本分别降低20.9%和24.1%,用于零射和蒸馏验证(表8).
在4B和27B时,经评估的仅决定的变式的票价估计值比其推理对应数低,但也低于Pass@1(表8)。
额外通行证@3和N=4 N=4 见附录C.1。

blocks.en: 5 Analysis: What Still Limits Verification?
blocks.zh: 5 分析:什么仍然有限度的核查?

blocks.en:
We analyze what distillation transfers from the GPT-5.6 Sol teacher using stored TMAX-9B trajectories from 21 held-out TMAX-15K tasks [ 1 ] , with N = 8 N=8 .
We use this offline benchmark to compare pairwise verification outputs of different models under the same state.
These diagnostics measure teacher agreement on verification, not action correctness or trajectory success.
blocks.zh:
我们分析GPT-5.6的蒸馏转移。 索尔教师使用储存的TMAX-9B轨迹,这些轨迹来自21项搁置的TMAX-15K任务[1],其中N=8N=8。
我们使用这一离线基准比较同一状态下不同模型的对偶核查结果。
这些诊断方法衡量的是教师关于核查的协议,而不是行动正确性或轨迹成功。

blocks.en:
Pairwise agreement is the fraction of comparisons with matching verifier and teacher A/B/TIE preferences.
For verification agreement , we count each candidate’s wins in the pairwise comparisons separately for both models, then measure the fraction of states where they identify the same top-ranked candidate. Appendix D.1.1 provides calculation details.

对于核查协议,我们将每个候选人的胜负分别计算在两种模式的对等比较中,然后衡量他们确定同一排名最高候选人的州的比例。 附录D.1.1提供了计算细节。

blocks.en: 5.2 Remaining Verification Challenges

blocks.en:
Verification agreement improves in every turn bin ( Figure 4 (a)).
It reaches 68.13% at turns 1-4 and 54.07% at turns 17-32, showing that the gains persist beyond the opening decisions while substantial disagreement remains later in the trajectory.

它在1至4轮达到68.13%,在17至32轮达到54.07%,表明收益持续到开放决定之后,而重大分歧则在轨迹较后期。

blocks.en:
We use GPT-5.6 Terra [ 18 ] to review teacher disagreements and classify those it judges clear verifier failures using a predefined taxonomy.
As in Figure 4 (b), the number of such cases falls from 3,328 for zero-shot verification to 1,810 after distillation, with fewer cases in every category.
Candidate semantics and execution feasibility account for 67.4% of these distilled-verifier cases.

blocks.en: 7 Related Work
blocks.zh: 7 相关工作

blocks.en:
Prior work develops agent interfaces [ 7 , 8 ] , context management [ 34 ] , and automated harness optimization [ 35 ] .
Model-side work scales supervised and reinforcement learning with synthetic tasks [ 36 , 37 , 38 , 1 , 39 ] .
Mid-Harness studies action scaling with the model and harness fixed.

模型侧工作尺度监督与强化学习与合成任务[36,37,38,1,39].

blocks.en:
Test-time compute scaling improves reasoning tasks with aggregation [ 40 ] , verification [ 11 , 24 , 16 ] , and search [ 41 , 42 ] .
Process reward models evaluate intermediate steps [ 21 ] , including through generative verification [ 43 , 44 ] , while V 1 V_{1} uses pairwise comparisons and tournaments to verify mathematical and code solutions [ 23 ] .
Although most works focus on reasoning tasks, our work mainly addresses agentic tasks and action scaling where each action affects the environment.
blocks.zh:
测试时间计算比例可改进推理任务,包括汇总[40]、核查[11、24、16]和搜索[41、42]。

尽管大多数工作都集中在推理任务上,但我们的工作主要是处理代理任务和每项行动都会影响环境的行动规模。

blocks.en:
Parallel verification [ 14 , 2 ] and sequential refinement [ 12 , 3 ] scale complete trajectories.
LLM-as-a-Verifier also verifies per-step candidates on Terminal-Bench [ 2 ] . Zainullina et al. [13] combine action ranking by a trained critic with trajectory selection for SWE tasks.
We instead study verification mechanisms using the generator as verifier across broader terminal tasks.
Other methods evaluate completed patches [ 45 , 46 ] or provide feedback during execution on SWE tasks [ 47 ] .
blocks.zh:
平行核查[14,2]和顺序改进[12,3] 尺度完整轨迹.
LLM-as-a-验证器还验证了终端-Bench上的每步候选人[2]. Zainullina et al. [13] 将训练有素的批评家的动作排名与SWE任务的轨迹选择结合起来.
相反,我们研究核查机制,利用发电机作为更广泛的终端任务的核查器。
其他方法评价已完成的补丁[45,46]或在执行SWE任务期间提供反馈[47].

blocks.en: 8 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8 结论

blocks.en:
We study action scaling for long-horizon terminal agents with the generator and harness fixed.
Useful alternatives from the same generator can improve trajectory success, but wider sampling yields little benefit under weak verification.
Pairwise comparison performs best among the evaluated mechanisms, and distilling the frontier model’s responses further improves success without changing the generator.
These gains extend across agent settings, while composition with trajectory scaling reaches higher success at lower estimated token cost than generating more trajectories alone.
These findings establish action scaling as a complementary axis of test-time compute scaling.
blocks.zh:
我们研究长视航站楼的操作缩放 并固定发电机和操纵装置
同一发电机的有用替代品可以改善轨迹的成功,但在核查不力的情况下,更广泛的取样没有产生什么好处。
在评估的机制中进行对等比较效果最好,对前沿模型的反应进行提炼,在不改变生成器的情况下进一步提高成功率。
这些收益跨越代理环境,而轨迹放大的构成以较低的估计象征性成本取得更高的成功,而不是仅仅产生更多的轨迹。
这些结论将行动规模确定为试验时间计算规模的一个补充轴。

blocks.en:
Distillation leaves a substantial gap to frontier verification, motivating better training algorithms such as reinforcement learning for verifiers [ 23 ] .
Our evaluation lacks gold action labels, limiting direct measurement of verification correctness and candidate coverage. Appendix A discusses these limitations and future directions in detail.
blocks.zh:
稀释给边界核查留下了很大的空白,促使核查人员进行强化学习等更好的培训算法。

blocks.en: Ethics statement
blocks.zh: 道德操守说明

blocks.en: Our experiments evaluate terminal agents in isolated benchmark environments. The action reliability studied here concerns successful task completion and does not establish the safety or security of generated commands. Improvements in terminal-agent capabilities may benefit legitimate automation but could also facilitate harmful activities. Deployment should therefore retain safeguards such as restricted permissions, environment isolation, and human approval for sensitive or irreversible actions. Action verification should complement these safeguards, not replace them.
blocks.zh: 我们的实验评估了孤立的基准环境中的终端剂. 这里研究的动作可靠性涉及任务的成功完成,没有确定生成命令的安全性或保障性. 终端代理能力的提高可能有利于合法的自动化,但也有利于有害的活动。 因此,部署应保留限制许可、环境隔离和人类批准敏感或不可逆转行动等保障措施。 行动核查应补充而不是取代这些保障措施。

blocks.en: Appendix A Limitations and Future Work
blocks.zh: 附录A 限制和今后的工作

blocks.en:
With the same TMAX-9B generator and eight candidates on TerminalBench-Lite, the distilled verifier reaches 57.14% Pass@1, compared with 68.03% for frontier verification ( Figure 2 ).
Our distillation approach transfers part of the frontier verifier’s capability but does not establish how to close this gap.
Command semantics and execution feasibility dominate the reviewed verifier failures, while teacher agreement remains lower in later states ( Figure 4 ).
These findings motivate learning from observed command outcomes and improving how verifiers represent task progress, unresolved requirements, and relevant history.
Future work could use a world model to predict action effects [ 48 ] , or jointly train generation and verification through reinforcement learning, following V 1 V_{1} [ 23 ] , so that the verifier adapts to the generator’s evolving action distribution.
blocks.zh:
使用同样的TMAX-9B发电机和终端Bench-Lite上的8名候选人,蒸馏的核查器达到57.14%的Pass@1,而用于边界核查的比分为68.03%(图2)。
我们的蒸馏方法转移了边境核查员的部分能力,但没有确定如何弥合这一差距。
指令语义和执行可行性在经过审查的核查失败中占主导地位,而教师协议在后来的各州仍然较低(图4)。
这些调查结果激励人们学习所观察到的指挥结果,改进核查者如何代表任务进展、尚未解决的要求和相关历史。
未来的工作可以使用世界模型来预测行动效果[48],或者通过强化学习,在V 1 V_{1}[23]之后联合训练生成和核查,这样核查者就可以适应生成者不断变化的行动分布.

blocks.en:
Our evaluation lacks gold action labels, limiting direct measurement of verification correctness, candidate coverage, and trajectory success attainable with perfect verification.
Mathematical reasoning benefits from step-level annotations and process reward models [ 21 , 28 , 49 ] , but collecting comparable evidence for terminal actions requires accounting for their effects on the environment.
Unlike response or trajectory verification, which can reuse sampled outputs [ 16 , 10 , 44 , 2 ] , changing an executed action changes subsequent states and candidate sets.
Our online comparisons therefore require new environment runs, and re-evaluating a fixed trajectory collection cannot establish performance under a different verifier.
Branching from intermediate states could support richer evaluation and tree or beam search, but requires environment cloning or restoration [ 41 , 50 ] .
blocks.zh:
我们的评价缺乏金色行动标签,限制了直接衡量核查的正确性、候选覆盖面和通过完美核查而能够实现的轨迹成功。
数学推理得益于阶梯级说明和过程奖励模型[21,28,49],但为终端行动收集可比证据需要对其对环境的影响进行核算.
与反应或轨迹验证不同,它们可以重复采样输出[16,10,44,2],改变已执行的动作会改变后续状态和候选组合.
因此,我们的在线比较需要新的环境运行,重新评价固定轨迹收集不能在不同的核查人下确定性能。
来自中间邦的分支可以支持更丰富的评价和树或梁的搜索,但需要环境克隆或恢复[41,50].

blocks.en:
We keep the generator’s reasoning settings fixed and do not compare action scaling with increasing reasoning effort for a single candidate [ 51 ] .
Generators with controllable reasoning effort could enable comparisons at comparable inference costs and tests of whether these allocations are complementary.
Our evaluated configurations also sample and verify at every action step, leaving open how to retain their gains with less compute.
Adaptive verification could vary candidate width and comparison effort across steps, motivated by adaptive stepwise scaling [ 52 ] .
Direct prediction through classification heads or single-token responses, as in process reward models [ 21 ] and decision-specific models such as Jev [ 53 ] , offers a way to reduce verifier decoding.
At N = 8 N=8 , decision-only verification improves TMAX-9B Pass@1 but reduces Pass@1 relative to reasoning-based verification at 4B and 27B ( Table 7 ).
Its lower reference-priced token cost can therefore come with a performance trade-off, although missing usage and separate live runs limit how precisely the comparison isolates the effect of response format ( Table 8 ).
blocks.zh:
我们保持发电机的推理设置的固定,不将动作缩放与一个候选人日益增加的推理努力进行比较[51].
具有可控推理能力的发电机可以比较可比推算成本,并测试这些分配是否相辅相成。
我们评价的配置在每一个动作步骤上也都进行抽样和核实,留下了如何用更少的计算来保留其收益的空洞余地.
适应性核查可能因适应性逐步缩小[52]而改变备选宽度和跨步骤的比较努力。
通过分类头直接预测或单键响应,如过程奖励模型[21]和Jev[53]等特定决策模型,提供了减少核查器解码的方法.
在 N = 8 N = 8 时,仅决定验证可以改善TMAX-9B Pass@1,但相对于基于推理的验证,在 4B 和 27B (表 7) 时减少 Pass@1 .
因此,其参考价格较低的代号成本可带来性能权衡,尽管缺少使用量和单独的直播量限制了比较如何准确隔离反应格式的影响(表8)。

blocks.en:
Our study focuses on terminal agents and on supervised verifier distillation with TMAX models.
Verifiers may further benefit from training methods studied in related settings, such as reasoning, agent, and vision-language model distillation [ 54 , 55 , 56 , 57 , 58 , 59 , 60 ] , self-distillation [ 61 ] , and reinforcement learning and search-based training [ 62 , 63 , 64 , 65 , 66 , 67 , 68 ] .
Tools and external knowledge [ 69 , 70 , 71 , 72 , 73 ] , together with techniques for managing context, memory, and multi-turn interaction [ 74 , 75 , 76 , 77 , 78 , 79 , 80 , 81 ] , could further inform verification, and verifier rationales could in turn serve as feedback for refinement [ 82 ] .
Advances in efficient model design and adaptation [ 83 , 84 , 85 , 86 , 87 , 88 , 89 ] may yield more compact verifiers, while causal and robustness analyses [ 90 , 91 , 92 , 93 , 94 , 95 ] could help characterize verifier behavior beyond task success.
Future work could test whether Mid-Harness improves agents for computer use [ 96 , 97 ] and robotics [ 98 , 99 , 100 ] .

我们的研究重点是终端剂和带有TMAX模型的有监督的核查器蒸馏。
验证者可进一步受益于相关环境下研究的培训方法,如推理、代理和视觉语言模型蒸馏[54、55、56、57、58、59、60]、自我消化[61]、强化学习和搜索培训[62、63、64、65、66、67、68]。
工具和外部知识[69、70、71、72、73],连同管理上下文、记忆和多回合互动的技术[74、75、76、77、78、79、80、81],可以进一步为核查提供参考,核查理由反过来可以作为改进的反馈[82]。
高效模型设计和适应方面的进展[83、84、85、86、87、88、89]可能会产生更紧凑的核实者,而因果性和强健性分析[90、91、92、93、94、95]则有助于描述核查者行为超越任务成功的范围。
今后的工作可以检验中Harness是否改进了计算机使用的代理[96,97]和机器人[98,99,100].

Pointwise verification scores each candidate independently and returns the highest-scoring action.
Listwise verification presents the full set and returns one choice.
Pairwise verification compares two actions, returns a preference and scores for both, and aggregates preferences using margin-weighted win rates.
The main mechanism comparisons use one listwise verifier call and the pairwise configurations in Table 3 . Full prompt templates and output formats are provided in Appendix B.6 .

blocks.en:
We follow the pivot tournament method introduced in Kwok et al. [2] .
A seeded shuffle arranges the M M candidates in a cycle. Adjacent candidates, including the last and first, are compared in parallel.
After these comparisons finish, candidates are ranked by their normalized ring scores, with seeded priorities breaking ties.
The top K ′ = min ⁡ ( K , M ) K^{\prime}=\min(K,M) candidates become pivots.
The pivot stage compares each non-pivot with every pivot and each unordered pair of pivots, with a seeded random A/B orientation for each comparison.
Pairs already scheduled in the ring are removed regardless of orientation.
Thus, overlapping ring-pivot pairs are not called again, and each existing ring record contributes only once to final aggregation.
The remaining pivot comparisons run in parallel after pivot selection, so ring and pivot are two sequential stages.
For eight distinct candidates and four pivots, this produces 22–25 comparisons, depending on the pivots’ positions in the ring.

blocks.en:
For verifier distillation, GPT-5.6 Sol generates a comparison rationale followed by scores and a preference label for each pair.
Supervision is collected from difficult tasks drawn from TMAX-15k, with three trajectories per task generated by TMAX-9B.
A trajectory contains about 20 steps on average, and intermediate states supply multiple verifier inputs.
After filtering and balancing, the finalized pairwise verification corpus retains 244 training tasks and 21 held-out analysis tasks, with 117,631 and 10,543 verifier inputs, respectively.
The analysis tasks are disjoint from training and are used only for the final analysis in Section 5 , not for checkpoint selection or training configuration.
Within each split, deterministic majority downsampling balances displayed A/B winners (seed 42), retaining all TIE examples.
This produces 56,274 A and 56,274 B examples plus 5,083 TIE examples for training. The analysis split contains 5,019 A, 5,019 B, and 505 TIE examples.

blocks.en: B.5 Evaluation Effort

blocks.en:
Each terminal-agent trial requires a fresh Docker environment and a sequence of model calls interleaved with command execution, so additional repetitions repeat an entire interactive trajectory.
Mid-Harness further generates multiple candidates and verifier responses at each action step.
Terminal-Bench [ 101 ] reports execution time, model-call counts, and token usage, with some trials lasting up to two hours and involving hundreds of model calls.
It also reports resolution rates with 95% confidence intervals and evaluates each supported agent–model combination at least five times.
Our evaluation uses three runs per task across the configurations studied. The cost of repeated interactive execution constrains further replication, motivating explicit reporting of uncertainty alongside observed performance gains.

中Harness在每一个行动步骤上进一步产生多个候选人和核实者的回应.
终端-Bench [101] 报告执行时间,模式召唤计数,以及象征性使用,有些试验长达两个小时,涉及数百个模式召唤.
它还报告95%置信间隔的解析率,并至少5次评估每个支持的代理-模型组合。
我们的评价工作在所研究的组合中采用每项任务三次运行。 重复互动执行的费用制约了进一步的复制,促使人们明确报告不确定性以及观察到的业绩收益。

We quantify uncertainty in the Base agent versus Mid-Harness comparisons in Figure 6 using the same 98 TerminalBench-Lite tasks and three runs per task for each configuration.
For each task, we compute the difference between the two configurations’ mean success rates over three runs.
We resample the 98 paired task blocks 100,000 times and report percentile 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for the mean difference.
This preserves pairing by task and keeps its repeated runs together, rather than treating 294 runs as independent tasks.
The intervals are marginal intervals for each comparison, not simultaneous intervals across all six comparisons.

Relative to the base agent, distilled Mid-Harness improves Pass@1 at all three model sizes in software engineering, machine learning, debugging, and system setup.
The software-engineering gains are 2.6, 5.1, and 20.5 percentage points for 4B, 9B, and 27B, respectively.
Other domains show mixed effects: on scientific-computing tasks, distilled verification improves 4B and 9B but reduces 27B Pass@1 by 10.0 points.

For each model and task, we take the median number of observed base-agent shell calls over three runs, excluding completion-marker commands.

blocks.en:
Each pair contributes two candidate scores and one absolute score gap.
Paired score MAE averages the absolute teacher-student difference for each candidate on its matched pair.
Repeated candidate appearances across pairs are retained, giving 20,394 score observations and 10,197 gaps. Figure 11 shows the discrete marginal proportions.
The joint heatmap in Figure 12 preserves candidate A/B orientation and uses a shared linear percentage scale, with each panel summing to 100%.
Its cells describe the two scores assigned by one model, rather than a teacher-versus-student confusion matrix.
These integer scores are comparative ratings, not calibrated task-success probabilities.

For verification diagnostics in Section 5 , we retain states whose every comparison is valid for both models.

The remaining 269 states (16.6%) are excluded because at least one stored comparison is invalid for either model.
Verification agreement is therefore conditional on complete valid responses at the state level.
States are grouped into turn bins 1–4, 5–8, 9–16, 17–32, and 33+.
The bins contain 182, 178, 388, 442, and 165 states, respectively.
The first four bins cover 21 tasks each, while the final bin covers eight.
All valid states within a bin are pooled, without task-macro weighting.

blocks.en:
We compute both agreement metrics from saved verifier and teacher responses, without executing candidate actions.
Pairwise agreement is the fraction of comparisons where their A/B/TIE preferences match.
For verification agreement, we count each candidate’s wins in the saved ring comparisons at each state, separately for the verifier and teacher.
An A/B preference gives the preferred candidate one win, while TIE gives neither candidate a win.
We identify the candidate with the most wins for each model, breaking ties by choosing the candidate that appears first in the original candidate order.
Verification agreement is the fraction of retained states where the verifier and teacher identify the same candidate.
This offline calculation uses win counts rather than the margin-weighted scores used during online execution ( Section 2.2 ).

blocks.en: Figure 4 (b) in the main text summarizes these analyses.

blocks.en:
Candidate semantics concerns the effect of a command or code change, and execution feasibility concerns whether it can execute as intended in the current environment.
Visible evidence concerns use of available observations, action phase concerns the timing or role of an action, and redundancy concerns repeated work.
Requirement and premature-completion failures concern unresolved task conditions and unsupported completion.
We review teacher disagreements from the zero-shot and distilled verifiers using GPT-5.6 Terra [ 18 ] .
The judge first assesses whether the teacher preference is unambiguous and well supported by the available evidence.
Only disagreements meeting this criterion are treated as clear verifier failures for this analysis and assigned one primary category from the predefined taxonomy above. Figure 4 (b) reports 3,328 zero-shot and 1,810 distilled cases passing this review, not the total numbers of teacher disagreements.
Candidate semantics and execution feasibility account for 1,926 zero-shot cases and 1,220 distilled cases, the latter comprising 67.4% of the reviewed distilled-verifier failures.
These are model-judged failures relative to a teacher reference, not independently established action errors or observed trajectory failures.

The task requires implementing a Go acoustic simulation solver, passing its regression test, and leaving an HTTP service listening on port 9090.
At turn 30, the regression test passes, but the visible state does not establish a running listener.
Candidate A builds and launches a server binary.
Candidate B runs a python3 -c command that scans process command lines and includes the following cleanup logic before a planned nohup launch: ⬇ with open ( f ’/ proc /{ pid }/ cmdline ’, ’ r ’) as f : cmdline = f . read () if ’9090’ in cmdline or ’ main . go ’ in cmdline : print ( f ’ Killing PID { pid }: { cmdline [:100]}’) os . kill ( int ( pid ), 9) The embedded Python command itself contains both matching strings, and the scan excludes neither its own process nor the invoking shell.

The distilled verifier acknowledges broad process matching but prefers B with scores 5 versus 7, rewarding its port check and persistent launch.
